decisions.reason: The published Frobenius definition sums all entries with zero-based labels; setting x_{ij}=a_{i-1,j-1} reindexes that finite sum as i=1..m, j=1..n. F1 and step 1.1 therefore give the same entrywise Euclidean norm. Steps 1.2 and 1.3 correctly identify each column block, including B transpose rather than adjoint over C, and step 2.1 adds the identities. This is a coordinate convention, not a missing dependency or inference.

The Definition gave only finite upper bounds N_A<=c_0*m and N_B<=c_0*n. For example -1 or 1/2 satisfies an appropriate upper bound but violates the nonnegative-integer N input of alg-finite-budget-francis-schur-reduction. Thus step 1 was not a defined delegated call on all expressly admitted inputs. Requiring nonnegative integer N_A,N_B repairs this logical input-domain defect while preserving both size caps, zero-budget cases, controller modes, exact certificates, pivot tests and all successful solves.
